transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because my primary doctor seems concerned that my meal planning has gotten a little too tight. Honestly, I don't really see it that way. To me, it just feels like... well, keeping breakfast to a yogurt, skipping lunch if I’m busy, and making a very measured dinner. It just makes sure the day stays orderly. I'm not exactly sure why she's so worried about it, but she wanted me to come see you.
When it comes to your meal planning, how much of this is driven by thoughts or worries about your body weight or shape?

Well, I suppose a fair amount of it is driven by my weight. I just... I like to know exactly where I stand. If I step on the scale and it's up even a pound, say, after eating a normal dinner or going out to a restaurant, I just feel this sharp panic. It feels like I've completely lost control. So, the meal planning is really just my way to make sure I can correct it the next day and get things back in order.
Do you ever have times where you eat an unusually large amount of food all at once and feel completely unable to stop?

No, not at all. I don't... I don't really have times like that. Eating a large amount of food all at once is exactly what I'm trying to avoid. I prefer to keep everything very small and measured. So, no, I've never had a moment where I felt like I couldn't stop eating.
To help me get a clearer picture of your health, could you tell me your current height and weight?

I'm 5 foot 4. And... right now, I weigh 98 pounds. My primary doctor told me that's too low, and I know it's drifted down more than she'd like. But honestly, when I look at the chart, I still find myself thinking that a little lower would just be a cleaner, more manageable number for me.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle, such as your periods becoming irregular or stopping altogether?
Well, I went through menopause years ago, so I haven't had a period in quite a long time. So, no, I haven't noticed any recent changes like that.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you see yourself as overweight or feel that parts of your body are too large?

Well, yes, I do. I know I'm an older woman, and I'm certainly not trying to look young or anything like that. But I still... I still judge how well I'm handling myself by how I look. When I look in the mirror, I'm always checking to see if my waist and hips look contained in my clothes. If I feel like those areas are too large or spreading out, it really bothers me. So, yes, I do see parts of my body as being too big.
